facts.after: Compatible tabs share one leader connection, and a full server buffer disconnects the slow client.
facts.before: Tabs can create redundant event connections and the server drops events when a client buffer fills.
conditions: If either cross-tab primitive is unavailable, each visible tab keeps its own connection.
A hidden tab releases its connection after 30 seconds; offline and page-hide events stop it sooner.
Unknown visibility rejects the broadcast, while private delivery retains its owner or administrator boundary.
facts.mechanism: The browser combines Web Locks and BroadcastChannel; the hub frames one event and distributes its bytes.

facts.after: The handler sends a heartbeat only after 30 seconds without event data and exits on the hub disconnect signal.
facts.before: The previous handler emits periodic heartbeats and lacks the revised disconnect signal.
conditions: Retry uses full jitter with a cap that grows from 1 second to 30 seconds.
A connection that survives 60 seconds resets the retry delay.
A 401 response tries token refresh once before the general retry path.
Cross-tab sharing is an optimization, not guaranteed delivery or a durable event log.
The change adds cross-tab, concurrency, race, and benchmark source files without a new rendered control.
facts.mechanism: Event delivery resets the timer; reconnect invalidates active memo queries and user statistics.

limits: No cross-tab browser session, network recovery, race test, or benchmark ran for this preparation.
